data_sources: pcb-flex-cuts-explained.mdx § 'Why bother, when the case already has a mount style' — 'That is the situation on a PCB-mount or top-mount board: the PCB is screwed rigidly to the plate, and the plate is screwed rigidly to the case, with no compressible layer anywhere in the stack. Every joint in that chain is a hard joint.'

pcb-flex-cuts-explained.mdx § 'Why bother, when the case already has a mount style' — 'QK75 ... There's no gasket ring, no foam strip, no leaf-spring tab anywhere in the stack. Whatever give a typist feels on that board either comes from the switch itself or from flex engineered into the PCB — there's no third place for it to come from.'

pcb-flex-cuts-explained.mdx § 'Why bother, when the case already has a mount style' — 'The Bakeneko65 clamshells its case around a single perimeter o-ring, giving the whole plate-and-PCB assembly a few tenths of a millimeter of travel before anything gets stiff. ... a flex cut at the PCB level would be additive rather than foundational — a small, local softening layered on top of a mount that was already going to feel soft.'
